title: Oct 12 Results + Oct 13 Preview: Zero Wins, Two Lessons Learned
summary: Oct 12 went 0-2, but Oct 13 brings fresh data and the Rays at 53% probability.

content.value:
## Oct 12 Results: The Numbers Don't Lie

Let me hit you with the reality check: we went 0-2 yesterday. That's a 0.0% success rate, folks. Not the data story I wanted to tell, but transparency is what we do here. Both picks missed - the Dodgers fell to the Brewers despite our 50% projection, and the Rays couldn't deliver even with a 63% win probability backing them.

## The Data Debrief

Here's what the numbers tell us: the Rays pick at 63% confidence was our stronger play, but variance is part of the game. A 63% probability means we still expected them to lose 37 times out of 100. Yesterday was one of those 37. The Dodgers pick at exactly 50%? That's a coin flip - and the coin didn't land our way.

## Oct 13 Preview: Back to the Well

Look at this: we're running it back with the exact same matchup. Guardians at Rays, Round 2. But here's where it gets interesting - the pitching matchup has completely flipped. Yesterday's game featured different arms, and today we've got Parker Messick going for Cleveland against Tampa Bay's Freddy Peralta.

## The Pitching Matchup Analysis

Freddy Peralta brings a different statistical profile to the mound for Tampa Bay. Our model has the Rays at 53% - notably lower than yesterday's 63%, which tells you the pitcher variable is carrying significant weight in the calculation. Parker Messick counters for Cleveland, and the model sees this as a tighter contest than Sunday's game.

## Bottom Line

53% isn't screaming confidence, but it's above the 50% threshold where we see value. After an 0-2 day, the temptation is to chase or overcorrect. We're not doing that. We're sticking to the data, trusting the process, and letting the sample size play out. One day doesn't make a trend - but consistent methodology does.
